messages:
maya: Heads-up — our Python async client suddenly fails the streaming handshake in CI after we migrated the repo to Poetry. Local devs can't repro. Error is `401 unauthorized` from /v1/stream with the same token we use locally. Anyone seen poetry/pip/keyring interactions bite streaming auth before?

tom: did you run `poetry run python -m pip list` in CI vs locally? sometimes CI picks up system keyring or a different keyring backend.

maya: I ran that. CI had `keyring` 23.x installed via global runner image, local devs don't. Removing it locally makes no diff. CI log snippet:```
ERROR: Stream handshake failed: 401 Unauthorized
headers: {"authorization": "Bearer <redacted>", "content-type": "application/json"}
response: {"error":"invalid_api_key"}
```

eli: that looks like the token didn't get into the process. Could poetry's virtualenv isolation + runner secrets cause the env var not to be visible to the subprocess started by uvloop/asyncio?

maya: hmm we export REDWOOD_API_KEY in the job env. The same job image works for other repos.

sam (DevEx): Quick checklist: 1) confirm env var present inside the same process that imports redwood; 2) check if our SDK auto-keyring lookup overrides env; 3) try forcing auth method to env with REDWOOD_AUTH_METHOD=env.

maya: confirmed: printing os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'] in the test prints the value. When I run `python -c "import redwood; print(redwood.auth.get_default())"` in CI it prints `keyring://` backend path, not the env key. So sdk is preferring keyring.

eli: ah ok — keyring can override env if installed; Poetry lockfile pulled a different keyring backend into the venv that devs don't have. CI's global keyring package + poetry-created venv combination weirdness.

sam (DevEx): Workarounds: 1) set REDWOOD_AUTH_METHOD=env in the CI job (forces env var use), 2) pin or remove keyring in pyproject to avoid auto-backend, or 3) call redwood.init(api_key=os.environ["REDWOOD_API_KEY"]) early in tests. I'd try #1 as low friction.

maya: tried #1 — setting REDWOOD_AUTH_METHOD=env fixed the handshake in CI. Tests passed. Will patch the repo to explicitly set that in the pipeline.

eli: long-term: we should add a note in SDK docs about credential precedence (env > explicit init > keyring) and a troubleshooting blurb about Poetry + keyring. Also consider an opt-out flag during init to skip keyring lookups.

sam (DevEx): I'll make a tiny docs PR and add a CI check snippet. Suggestion for PR text: "CI flaky auth with Poetry + keyring: set REDWOOD_AUTH_METHOD=env or pin keyring backend." I can open it unless you want to.

maya: please open it, thanks. Also filing a follow-up to investigate whether keyring should ever auto-win over an env var — that feels surprising.

sam (DevEx): FYI I've added a short snippet for the docs and a template CI fix in the devex repo. Will link PR in thread when ready. :thumbsup:
